Interface-declared (2 impls + test doubles). A bool predicate, phrased in the third person to pair with its sibling audits(object): bool. The is_/has_ prefixes read badly here (is_parameters_captured).

The class doc already calls this pair 'encode'/'revive', and it pairs with is_encoded(). The literal alternative is to_payload()/from_payload(), on the 0.6 to_array/from_array pattern. Call sites: ddd-sf ProcessRowCodec, ddd-wp ProcessRepository, IntegrationBehaviour.
A static named constructor; it throws UndecodableLargeString, so the name 'decode' matches the exception. Rename together with toPayload->encode, or neither.
Matches the stored max_bytes key and OutboxConfig::$max_payload_bytes. Also a named constructor argument (maxBytes:) at call sites.

It holds exactly the constructor's $reason, without the 'Undecodable LargeString:' message prefix. The host stores it as quarantine_reason, and the docblock should say so. Alternative: quarantine_reason, for parity with the column and with InMemoryProcessStore::quarantineReasonOf (process area).
The 'ref' abbreviation matches InMemoryOutboxStore::transportRefOf (outbox area), assumed to become transport_ref_of.

Interface-declared (8 impls, including TXP and conformance fixtures). A bare key() was rejected: it is too generic on a user command and could collide with a command property. Assumes WakeupIntent/ProcessWakeupMessage::idempotencyKey also become idempotency_key.

Interface-declared (8 impls). It returns the command dispatched once when the subscriber's budget is exhausted, and the docs already call that 'compensation'. Risk: process steps also use 'compensate/undo', for a different mechanism. Safe fallback: failure_command. Do not use on_exhausted (Subscriber::onExhausted, outbox area): that name reads as a hook, but this method returns a value.

reason: The _for_tests suffix is the deliberate guard: the class contract says production never clears host defaults, so a bare reset() would invite misuse.

reason: Keeps the shared _for_tests test-seam suffix and drops 'registrations' (register() is the class's only other input); reset_for_tests was avoided because 'reset' already means between_messages() on a class called RuntimeReset.

reason: Same one-shot test-control family as fail_next_commit.
